as_of_line: As of 2026-09-15 (night IST / daytime ET, US). The governing primary source remains NOAA CPC's ENSO Diagnostic Discussion issued 2026-09-10 (re-confirmed via direct fetch tonight, unchanged), next scheduled CPC update 2026-10-08. Latest secondary/wire coverage is dated 2026-09-14. WMO's most recent dedicated El Niño statement is 2026-09-03; no newer WMO bulletin found. BoM's ENSO Outlook page returned HTTP 403 to direct fetch again tonight (confirms the prior brief's block, not new data).
what_moved: Top-line CPC advisory status is UNCHANGED since Sept 10 (still >90% very-strong / 75% historic, next update Oct 8) — no new CPC issuance this week. What's new tonight from primary-source re-fetches: (1) the full Niño-region breakdown now includes Niño-3 (+2.5°C) and Niño-4 (+0.1°C), not just 3.4/1+2, showing the warmth is concentrated in the eastern Pacific while the far-west Niño-4 region sits near neutral; (2) climate.us's Sept 10 post quantifies the quiet Atlantic explicitly as hurricane activity running "less than 10% of normal"; (3) NHC's Sept 14 Atlantic Tropical Weather Outlook confirms the quiet-basin framing directly — no active storms, one area of interest near Bermuda at 40% (7-day) / near-0% (48-hr) formation odds, taken during what is climatologically the peak of the season (Sept 10); (4) WMO's Sept 3 release adds two granular data points not previously logged: subsurface Pacific temperatures up to 8°C above average and a positive Indian Ocean Dipole forecast (SON 2026 mean +0.9°C) compounding the pattern; (5) CPC's own 90-day outlook page confirms official seasonal outlooks are re-issued monthly near mid-month, meaning a fresh DJF 2026-27 map is due around Sept 18-19 (not yet out as of tonight). BoM's page stayed blocked (403) on a second direct attempt tonight — still no independently-read BoM primary text.

facts.fact: NHC's Atlantic Tropical Weather Outlook issued Sept 14, 2026 shows the basin quiet at the climatological peak of the season: no active tropical storms/hurricanes in the Atlantic, Caribbean, or Gulf; one disorganized area ~1,000 miles east-southeast of Bermuda.
facts.source_name: NOAA National Hurricane Center (NHC), Atlantic Tropical Weather Outlook

facts.fact: NHC puts that lone area of interest's formation odds at near-0% in 48 hours and 40% over 7 days, with conditions becoming 'more conducive for development by the middle of this week.'
facts.source_name: NOAA National Hurricane Center (NHC), Atlantic Tropical Weather Outlook

facts.fact: WMO's Sept 3 release puts the probability of El Niño persisting through February 2027 at roughly 100%.

facts.fact: WMO's Sept 3 release cites subsurface Pacific ocean temperatures up to 8°C above average in some areas (July-early August 2026) as the reservoir sustaining the event — a detail not in the prior brief.

facts.fact: WMO's Sept 3 release also forecasts a positive Indian Ocean Dipole for Sept-Nov 2026, seasonal mean value +0.9°C — a compounding factor not previously logged.
facts.source_name: World Meteorological Organization (WMO), news release

unknowns: CPC has not stated an exact projected peak Niño-3.4 value for winter — only probability bands (>90% very strong, 75% historic) pending the Oct 8 update.
BoM's ENSO Outlook page again returned HTTP 403 to direct automated fetch tonight (second consecutive session) — its current wording remains un-verified against a directly-read primary page.
No agency (CPC, WMO, BoM, NHC) has used the media nicknames 'super El Niño' or 'Godzilla El Niño' in its own text — those remain journalistic labels only.

NOAA has not yet issued its flagship 2026-27 Winter Outlook press release (expected October); the mid-September 90-day/DJF seasonal map update (due ~Sept 18-19 per CPC's own cadence) had also not posted with readable regional detail as of tonight's fetch (maps are image-based, not text-extractable via this session's tools).
No agency has stated a projected transition date to ENSO-neutral or La Niña after this event; WMO's persistence statement stops at 'through February 2027.'

CPC has not itself commented (in material reviewed this session) on the Pacific-hurricane-threat-to-Hawaii, Indonesia-wildfire, or Atlantic-quiet linkages that CNN and climate.us have drawn; those attributions come from the press/ENSO Blog, not a CPC statement.

No fresh WMO bulletin dated after Sept 3, 2026 was located this session (the WMO news portal's most recent El Niño-specific item is still the Sept 3 release); a Sept 14 'Pacific Meteorological Council' item exists but is about Pacific weather-readiness broadly, not a new ENSO statement.
